drug_class: Direct-acting antiviral (pangenotypic NS3/4A protease inhibitor + NS5A inhibitor combination)
purpose: This medication is used to treat chronic Hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection in adults and children who are at least 3 years old. It works against all major types (genotypes) of Hepatitis C. Treating Hepatitis C can help prevent serious liver problems like cirrhosis or liver cancer.
how_it_works: Hepatitis C is a virus that attacks your liver. This medicine is actually two medications combined — they work as a team to block two different tools the Hepatitis C virus needs to copy itself and spread. By blocking these tools, the medicine stops the virus from multiplying, allowing your body to clear the infection. Most people are cured after completing their full course of treatment.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are headache, tiredness, nausea, and diarrhea. Some people may also feel itchy or have stomach discomfort. These side effects are usually mild and tend to get better as your body adjusts to the medication.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you have severe liver disease (advanced cirrhosis) or if you are taking certain medications like rifampin, atazanavir, or certain cholesterol-lowering drugs (statins), as dangerous interactions can occur. If you have ever had Hepatitis B, tell your doctor right away — this medicine can cause Hepatitis B to reactivate and become serious. Always tell your doctor and pharmacist about every medication, supplement, or herbal product you take before starting this medicine.
typical_dosing: For most adults, the usual dose is 3 tablets taken together once a day with food, for 8 to 12 weeks depending on your specific situation and liver health. Taking it with a meal helps your body absorb the medicine better and can reduce stomach upset. Always finish the full course your doctor prescribes, even if you feel fine, to make sure the virus is fully cleared.
